title: Fidelity Adoption Lifecycle and Commercial Staging Brief
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Playbook that defines the lifecycle stages for customer adoption of fidelity tiers, and a commercial staging approach that aligns SLOs, telemetry, and pricing anchors for progressive rollout.
body:
Overview

This brief defines the Fidelity Adoption Lifecycle and the associated Commercial Staging model we will use to onboard customers onto tiered fidelity offerings. It combines operational SLO guidance, telemetry and eval requirements, pricing anchors, and a repeatable rollout playbook so Product, Growth, and Customer Success can coordinate low-friction transitions from trial to paid fidelity.

Objectives

- Provide a deterministic lifecycle model for fidelity adoption (Discovery -> Pilot -> Scale -> Commercial Staging -> Mature).
- Define measurable acceptance criteria and telemetry hooks at each stage.
- Provide pricing and packaging anchors that map directly to observed telemetry and economic inflection points.
- Minimize quality regressions during fidelity upgrades with explicit eval and rollback gates.

Audience

This document is intended for: product managers, solutions engineers, customer success leads, pricing, and the observability/telemetry team responsible for fidelity metrics.

Success metrics (initial targets)

- Pilot conversion rate: >= 35% (pilot -> paid tier within 90 days).
- Post-upgrade call latency (p95): no more than 1.5x baseline for the same model variant.
- Fidelity-related complaint rate: < 0.5% of customer requests in first 30 days after staged upgrade.
- Economic uplift: average revenue per customer (ARPC) increase of >= 18% for customers adopting premium fidelity packages within 6 months.

Lifecycle stages and acceptance criteria

1) Discovery (self-serve)
   - Goals: expose fidelity tiers in the developer sandbox, surface cost/latency previews, and capture baseline telemetry (per-route p50/p95, token distribution).
   - Acceptance criteria: developer can select a fidelity preset via console/SDK; telemetry shows at least 1,000 sample requests or 7 days of usage; auto-eval harness captures a representative prompt set.

2) Pilot (guided, time-boxed)
   - Goals: validate quality and cost tradeoffs on a customer-specific prompt corpus, exercise fallback and quantization variants.
   - Acceptance criteria: shadow-eval pass rate >= 95% for key prompt set or no more than 1% drop in critical task accuracy; cost delta vs baseline <= configured threshold (default 1.25x).

3) Scale (broad internal rollout)
   - Goals: move multiple internal teams or product areas onto fidelity tier while monitoring churn and load patterns.
   - Acceptance criteria: sustained throughput across routes, stable latency tail, no SLO breach for 14 consecutive days.

4) Commercial Staging (contracted pilots with billing)
   - Goals: map fidelity usage to pricing anchors and billing entitlements, validate billing reconciliation and entitlement enforcement.
   - Acceptance criteria: billing events reconcile within 24 hours in test environment; customers receive consolidated usage + fidelity credit report; SLA mapping in contract is reflected in runtime routing.

5) Mature (general availability)
   - Goals: full customer self-serve for fidelity selection, documented rollback and escalation paths, and cost/quality playbooks for CSMs.
   - Acceptance criteria: stable telemetry signals, positive NPS delta for fidelity adopters, demonstrated unit economics.

Observability & telemetry requirements

- Mandatory telemetry fields: route_id, model_variant, fidelity_preset, request_tokens, response_tokens, backend_ms, kv_cache_hit, fallback_reason (nullable), eval_score.
- Standard SLOs to surface in Console for fidelity-aware routes:
  - Availability: 99.95% (rolling 30d)
  - Latency (p95): configurable per fidelity tier; default mapping: baseline-tier <= 200ms, premium-tier <= 350ms
  - Error budget burn alert: 5% remaining triggers on-call notification and automated rate-limit ramp-down.
- Eval harness: every staged upgrade must run the tenant prompt-set through shadow-eval with metrics captured (BLEU/EM/ROUGE/custom accuracy as appropriate) and an automated comparison report generated.

Pricing and packaging guidance

- Pricing anchors (example starter template):
| Tier | Fidelity Preset | Price Multiplier vs Baseline | Typical Use Cases |
| BASIC | baseline | 1.0x | low-latency chat, short response embeddings |
| PLUS  | enhanced sampling | 1.4x | richer completions, high-variance outputs |
| PRIME | extended context + higher compute | 1.9x | high-quality summarization, compositional reasoning |

- Crediting and trials: pilot customers receive a staged fidelity credit pool (e.g., 100k premium tokens) that expires after 60 days; credits are consumed before billable units and visible in Console billing tab.
- Commercial staging discounts: for customers committing to >6 months of premium fidelity, offer 12% sliding discount and priority warm capacity for peak windows.

Regression & safety gates

- Automated rollback triggers (immediate): fidelity upgrade that causes a regression >5% on any primary business metric (e.g., conversion, classification accuracy) or an SLO breach >2% sustained for >60 minutes.
- Manual rollback: CSM or Solutions Engineer can initiate a rollback from the Console; runbook follows steps in section "Rollback procedure."

Rollback procedure (numbered, for ops and CSMs)

1. Verify telemetry anomaly and correlated eval failure via Console -> Fidelity Insights.
2. Open a staging rollback request and notify on-call SRE via PagerDuty tag "fidelity-regressions".
3. Trigger variant switch to previous fidelity preset using the runtime admin API: POST /admin/route/{route_id}/set-fidelity {"preset":"previous"}.
4. Validate rollback: run 100 synthetic requests from the tenant prompt set and confirm eval_score returns to baseline within tolerance.
5. Document incident, root cause, and next steps in product retro.

Operational runbook excerpts

- Admin API snippets (example):
  - Check current preset: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" https://runtime.redwood.ai/admin/route/1234 | jq '.fidelity_preset'
  - Stage new preset (dry-run): curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" -d '{"preset":"prime","dry_run":true}' https://runtime.redwood.ai/admin/route/1234/stage

Ownership and coordination matrix

- Product (owner): lifecycle model, acceptance criteria, pricing anchors, and consumer-facing docs.
- Solutions Engineering: pilot onboarding, customer-specific eval sets, technical enablement.
- Observability: telemetry schema, dashboards, and automated alerting.
- SRE/Serving Runtime: rollout APIs, canary mechanics, and capacity gating.
- Customer Success / GTM: commercial staging negotiations and playbook execution.

Risk analysis and mitigations

- Risk: fidelity upgrades drive excessive cost for customers without measurable quality gain. Mitigation: require pilot with cost delta thresholds and a mandatory cost/benefit report before commercial staging.
- Risk: billing reconciliation mismatches. Mitigation: end-to-end billing test cases and a 24-hour reconciliation SLA for staging contracts.
- Risk: model quality regressions post-quantization/optimization. Mitigation: mandatory shadow-eval and canary window of minimum 72 hours with both telem and human review.

Recommended 90-day rollout plan (high level)

Week 0-2: Finalize fidelity presets and telemetry schema; instrument developer sandbox to export sample prompt sets.
Week 3-6: Run 5 controlled pilots across different verticals (SaaS, search, summarization); collect conversion and quality metrics.
Week 7-10: Integrate billing credit flows, reconciliation tests, and Console exposure for fidelity credit balances.
Week 11-12: Open commercial staging to qualifying customers with documented SLA mappings and optional warm capacity entitlements.

Appendix: Example fidelity acceptance checklist (for each customer)

- Prompt set captured and uploaded (min 200 examples).
- Shadow-eval baseline generated and reviewed by Solutions Engineering.
- Billing credits applied and visible in Console.
- Warm capacity window scheduled (if requested).
- Rollback window and on-call contacts confirmed.

Related artifacts and next steps

- Action: Product to draft standard contract language for fidelity staging addendum (due 2026-05-15).
- Action: Observability to publish the Console Fidelity Insights dashboard template (due 2026-05-08).
- Action: Sales Enablement to create a one-pager for customers that summarizes upgrade benefits and credit mechanics (due 2026-05-20).
